title: Speculative micro-hash routing and compact prefix store to shrink prefill CPU and latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: A non-trivial portion of per-request CPU and end-to-end latency during prefill is spent in prompt preprocessing: UTF-8 segmentation, normalization, prefix lookup, and token-boundary detection. For short-to-medium prompts and high QPS use-cases (chat bursts, search reranks), the cost of repeated identical prefix work and branchy UTF-8 codepaths dominates. Existing approaches (global prefix caches, naive prewarm) either bloat memory or create cache churn under multi-tenant workloads.

Proposal: Implement a speculative prefill fastlane that combines three components: 1) a compact on-CPU prefix-store (compact prefix trie serialized into cache-line-aligned blocks) that maintains hot prompt prefixes per-tenant with a small LRU and bloom-guided fallback; 2) a micro-hash router that cheaply maps incoming request signatures (string hash of normalized first N chars + tenant id + route hints) to either: fastlane path (compact prefix match, vectorized segmentation) or slow path (full UTF-8 normalizer + full tokenization); 3) instrumentation-driven adaptive thresholds so frequent short messages stay on the fastlane while long/rare inputs automatically go to the slow comprehensive pipeline.

Implementation notes: compact prefix store will be stored per-worker in a shared read-mostly region to avoid lock contention. Use a 64-bit fingerprint (SipHash) + 8-bit length bucketing to index into fixed-size microbuckets; on-hit we run a block-aligned SIMD UTF-8 segmenter optimized for ASCII/latin-1 heavy inputs. Bloom filter is consulted before an expensive memcmp to reduce misses. The micro-hash router is intentionally probabilistic to enable speculative execution: when a request is routed to the fastlane but later fails to match, we can continue tokenization on the slow path while logging a mis-speculation metric for the adaptive controller.

Goals: reduce median prefill CPU cycles and P50 latency for common chat prompts, keep memory overhead modest (<8MB per worker), and provide clear observability to tune thresholds per-customer.

Tradeoffs considered: full global prefix cache (higher hit rate but large memory and eviction storms), aggressive prewarm (wastes CPU on cold tenants), and hardware-only approaches (require AVX availability). We favor a hybrid software-first approach with optional SIMD acceleration on supported machines.
acceptance_criteria: Median prefill CPU cycles for short prompts (<=128 chars) reduced by >=30% on benchmark cluster
P50 prefill latency reduction of >=20ms for our chat workload benchmark (default runtime config)
Memory overhead per worker for compact prefix store < 8MB under 95th percentile tenant cardinality
Observability: new metrics emitted (fastlane_hits, fastlane_mispred, fastlane_fallback_latency) and dashboards created
Gradual rollout plan documented with canary thresholds and automatic rollback on increased error or latency
End-to-end tests and integration test in CI that validates correctness vs slow tokenization for randomized synthetic inputs
tasks: Design compact prefix store serialization format and microbucket layout (spec RFC)
Implement micro-hash router and integrate with request ingress pipeline
Vectorized ASCII-first UTF-8 segmenter implementation with fallthrough to general normalizer
Add bloom-guided fallback and LRU eviction; ensure per-worker memory caps
Develop perf harness and benchmark scenarios (chat bursts, long-form prompts, multi-tenant churn)
Add observability, metrics, and dashboard tiles; wire up alerting for misprediction rate
Write CI integration tests comparing fastlane vs baseline tokenizer for correctness/safety
Run canary rollout on dedicated cluster, monitor for regressions, and collect cost delta
